passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
The Philistines captured David in Gath.
David gave this song to the choirmaster.
The choirmaster should use the tune called “A Dove on Distant Oaks.”
This song is a Miktam.

passages.text: Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
David wrote it when the Philistines captured him in Gath.
David gave this song to the choirmaster.
David called this song “A Dove on Distant Oaks.”
David said, “God, be merciful to me.”
Men are chasing me.
They attack me all day.
They press hard against me.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ׀ עַל־ י֬וֹנַת אֵ֣לֶם רְ֭חֹקִים לְדָוִ֣ד מִכְתָּ֑ם בֶּֽאֱחֹ֨ז אֹת֖וֹ פְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים בְּגַֽת׃ חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱ֭לֹהִים כִּֽי־ שְׁאָפַ֣נִי אֱנ֑וֹשׁ כָּל־ הַ֝יּ֗וֹם לֹחֵ֥ם יִלְחָצֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David is in danger.
The Philistines have seized David in Gath.
David has many enemies.
My enemies chase me all day.
Many people attack me with pride.
They do this without stopping.
passages.original: שָׁאֲפ֣וּ שׁ֭וֹרְרַי כָּל־ הַיּ֑וֹם כִּֽי־ רַבִּ֨ים לֹחֲמִ֖ים לִ֣י מָרֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm when the Philistines captured him in Gath.
David was a servant of God.
David often faced danger from his enemies.
David sometimes felt afraid.
When David felt fear, he chose to trust God.
David said, "When I am afraid, I trust in You, God."

passages.text: In God, whose word I praise— in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
passages.sermon:
God is the one I praise.
I praise His word.
I trust in God.
I do not feel afraid.
No person can harm me.
passages.original: בֵּאלֹהִים֮ אֲהַלֵּ֪ל דְּבָ֫ר֥וֹ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־ יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בָשָׂ֣ר לִֽי׃

passages.text: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise.
passages.sermon:
Enemies surround me.
They twist my words all day long.
They change what I say.
They do this constantly.
They think only about harming me.
They plan evil against me.
Their thoughts are always for my downfall.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַ֭יּוֹם דְּבָרַ֣י יְעַצֵּ֑בוּ עָלַ֖י כָּל־ מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֣ם לָרָֽע׃

passages.text: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.
passages.sermon:
My enemies conspire against me.
They hide and wait for me.
They watch every step I take.
They want to take my life.
passages.original: יָג֤וּרוּ׀ יַצְפִּינוּ הֵ֭מָּה עֲקֵבַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֑רוּ כַּ֝אֲשֶׁ֗ר קִוּ֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
passages.sermon:
God sees the sins of the people.
The people do evil things.
They hope to escape punishment.
God, show Your anger.
God, bring down the nations.
God, do not let them escape.
passages.original: עַל־ אָ֥וֶן פַּלֶּט־ לָ֑מוֹ בְּ֝אַ֗ף עַמִּ֤ים׀ הוֹרֵ֬ד אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle— are they not in Your book?
passages.sermon:
God knows me.
God sees everywhere I go.
God counts all my wanderings.
God notices every place I travel.
God keeps my tears.
God puts my tears in His bottle.
God records my pain.
God writes my tears in His book.
passages.original: נֹדִי֮ סָפַ֪רְתָּ֫ה אָ֥תָּה שִׂ֣ימָה דִמְעָתִ֣י בְנֹאדֶ֑ךָ הֲ֝לֹ֗א בְּסִפְרָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.
passages.sermon:
My enemies attack me.
I cry out for help.
On that day, my enemies will turn back.
They will retreat.
This shows me something important.
I know God is with me.
God is on my side.
passages.original: אָ֥֨ז יָ֘שׁ֤וּבוּ אוֹיְבַ֣י אָ֭חוֹר בְּי֣וֹם אֶקְרָ֑א זֶה־ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִֽי׃

passages.text: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
passages.sermon:
David wrote this when he fled from Saul into a cave.
David trusted God.
David praised God's word.
David praised the LORD's word.
David put his trust in God.
David said, "I will not be afraid."
David asked, "What can man do to me?"
passages.original: בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר בַּ֝יהוָ֗ה אֲהַלֵּ֥ל דָּבָֽר׃ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־ יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃

passages.text: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David is in danger.
David fled from Saul.
David hides in a cave.
David says, “O God, your vows are upon me.”
David promises to keep God’s vows.
David says, “I will give you thank offerings.”
David will thank God.
passages.original: עָלַ֣י אֱלֹהִ֣ים נְדָרֶ֑יךָ אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם תּוֹדֹ֣ת לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
passages.sermon:
God saved me from death.
God kept my feet from slipping.
Now I walk before God.
I walk in the light of life.
passages.original: כִּ֤י הִצַּ֪לְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֡י מִמָּוֶת֮ הֲלֹ֥א רַגְלַ֗י מִ֫דֶּ֥חִי לְ֭הִֽתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים בְּ֝א֗וֹר הַֽחַיִּֽים׃
